# Welcome to ArunCode

ArunCode is a suite of tools built by **Arun Chandrasekaran**.

## What's Included

- **ArunCode_Term** — A terminal environment for managing your system
- **ArunCode IDE** — A full code editor with file saving and folder creation
- **ArunCode_Emails** — Send and receive messages between users
- **Python Teaching Club** — Learn Python with lessons and quizzes
- **ArunCode Docs** — You are here!

## Getting Started

1. Log in at `/terminal`
2. You'll be taken to your dashboard at `/home`
3. Click any app card to launch it
4. Admin users have access to the Admin Panel and Security Manager

## Roles

| Role | Permissions |
|---|---|
| admin | Full access — edit docs, manage users |
| security | View users, access logs, delete regular users |
| user | Access all apps, read docs |

---

*Version 5.0.0 — Created 2026*
title: Welcome to ArunCode

# ArunCode_Term Guide

ArunCode_Term is the terminal dashboard application.

## Logging In

1. Go to `/terminal`
2. Enter your email and username
3. Enter your password
4. **Admin accounts** require a 6-digit PIN as a second factor

## Dashboard Commands

Once logged in, you can use the built-in terminal widget:

```
help     — show all commands
status   — system status
version  — current version
whoami   — logged in user
date     — current date/time
ide      — open ArunCode IDE
logout   — end your session
clear    — clear the console
```

## Version History

Access the full version history at `/about/versions/versionhistory.html`
title: ArunCode_Term Guide

# ArunCode IDE

A browser-based code editor with file saving and folder support.

## Features

- **Syntax highlighting** for Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, JSON
- **Multiple tabs** — open several files at once
- **File tree** sidebar
- **Save to server** — files persist in the `workspace/` folder
- **Create folders** — organise your projects
- **Run code** — execute JavaScript directly, simulate Python output
- **Line numbers** with gutter sync

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Insert 4 spaces |
| Enter (in toolbar) | Confirm action |

## Saving Files

Files are saved server-side in the `workspace/` directory next to `app.py`.
They persist across sessions.

## Running Code

- **JavaScript** — executes live in the browser, output shown in console
- **Python** — simulates `print()` output (no real Python runtime in browser)
title: IDE User Guide

# Python Teaching Club

Learn Python through structured lessons with quizzes.

## Lessons

| # | Title | Level |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | Hello, Python! | Beginner |
| 02 | Variables & Data Types | Beginner |
| 03 | If Statements | Beginner |
| 04 | Loops | Intermediate |
| 05 | Functions | Intermediate |

## How to Use

1. Go to `/ptc`
2. Click any lesson card to open it
3. Read through the lesson content and code examples
4. Answer the quiz question at the bottom
5. Click **MARK AS DONE** to track your progress

## Leaderboard

Points are tracked and shown on the leaderboard tab.
Earn points by completing lessons and quizzes.
title: Python Teaching Club

# ArunCode Emails

An internal messaging system between ArunCode users.

## Sending an Email

1. Go to `/emails`
2. Click **+ COMPOSE**
3. In the **To** field, enter a **username** (e.g. `ArunC`) or their email address
4. Fill in Subject and body
5. Click **SEND**

> Emails are stored on the server in `emails.json` and persist permanently.

## Inbox

- **Unread** emails are highlighted with a purple dot
- Click an email to read it — it will be marked as read automatically
- Use the **↩ REPLY** button to reply to a message

## Folders

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| Inbox | Emails sent to you |
| Sent | Emails you sent |
| Starred | Emails you starred with ⭐ |

## Limitations

- Emails only work between ArunCode users (not external Gmail etc.)
- No attachments currently supported
title: Email System Guide

# Arduino Help

This section explains how to set up, install tools, upload code, and use the Arduino rover.

## Setup Hardware

1. Connect your Arduino to your computer using USB
2. Connect your motor driver and rover wires to:
   - Pin 4
   - Pin 5
   - Pin 6
   - Pin 7
3. Ensure your rover has power (battery or external supply)

---

## Install Arduino IDE

### Option 1: Download (Recommended)

1. Go to:
   https://www.arduino.cc/en/software
2. Download Arduino IDE (Linux, Windows, or Mac)
3. Install and open it

---

### Option 2: Install via Terminal (Linux / ChromeOS)

Run:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install arduino

If that fails (older version), install manually:
1. Download from arduino.cc
2. Extract the file
3. Run:
./arduino-ide

---

## First-Time Setup

1. Open Arduino IDE
2. Go to:
   Tools → Board → Arduino UNO
3. Plug in Arduino
4. Select port:
   Tools → Port → /dev/ttyACM0 (or similar)

Check ports with:
ls /dev/ttyACM*

---

## Upload Code

1. Open your `.ino` file
2. Click the ✔ (Verify) button to compile
3. Click the → (Upload) button

---

## Upload via Terminal (Advanced)

Install CLI:
sudo apt install arduino-cli

Setup:
arduino-cli core update-index
arduino-cli core install arduino:avr

Compile:
arduino-cli compile --fqbn arduino:avr:uno your_file.ino

Upload:
arduino-cli upload -p /dev/ttyACM0 --fqbn arduino:avr:uno your_file.ino

---

## Commands

Edit this line in the code:
Command = "Move Forward";

Available commands:
- "Move Forward"
- "Move Backwards"
- "Turn Right"
- "Turn Left"

---

## Direction

Edit:
Dir = "Clockwise";

Options:
- "Clockwise" → normal direction
- "Counter Clockwise" → reverse direction

---

## Movement Logic

- Forward: both motors move forward
- Backward: both motors reverse
- Turn Right: left motor moves
- Turn Left: right motor moves

---

## Troubleshooting

Problem: Upload fails  
Fix:
- Close Serial Monitor
- Check correct port
- Replug Arduino

Check port usage:
lsof /dev/ttyACM0

---

Problem: Permission denied  
Fix:
sudo usermod -a -G dialout $USER
(restart after)

---

Problem: Rover not moving  
Fix:
- Check wiring
- Check power supply
- Try switching HIGH/LOW values

---

Problem: Moves wrong direction  
Fix:
- Change "Clockwise" to "Counter Clockwise"
- Or swap motor wires

---

## Notes

- Pins 0 and 1 should not be used (Serial)
- Always double-check wiring
- Code runs continuously in loop()
